Hi Maya / Atlas IT team —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. I wanted to capture the proposed orchestration plan for enterprise access during the onboarding so everyone (internal + Atlas) has the same expectations. This thread will be our single source for the technical handoff items.

High-level asks we need to confirm this week:
- SSO (SAML): ACS/Entity ID and expected NameID/attribute mapping
- SCIM: user/group attributes you want synced and who owns group mapping decisions
- IP allowlist: production test & staging egress IPs and cutover window (we will request whitelist from Atlas)
- Service accounts: naming, least-privilege roles, and rotation policy
- Org policies: any SCIM rate limits, SCIM token expiry, or user provisioning constraints

I've attached an implementation_checklist.xlsx with owner columns — please review and flag anything missing.

Suggested timeline (flexible):
- 9/1: finalize SAML/SCIM attribute spec, firewall IP list
- 9/3–9/6: test SAML & SCIM against Atlas test tenant, service account provisioning
- 9/8: staged cutover and monitoring window

Jonas, can you verify SAML/SCIM technical recommendations and provide the sample artifacts? Karthik/Ben — please confirm who will own service account provisioning and IP whitelist requests respectively.

Maya / Procurement — let us know if the service account naming/privileges are subject to a procurement approval; we can align timeline accordingly.

Thanks,

Thanks Neha — posting the technical delta and attachments here so Atlas IT has a concrete starting point.

Quick SAML notes (recommended):
- Assertion Consumer Service (ACS): https://api.redwood.ai/sso/atlasbank/acs
- SP Entity ID: https://api.redwood.ai/sso/atlasbank
- NameID: persistent; format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress
- Recommended attributes: email, given_name, family_name, groups (string array)
- Signature: RSA-SHA256, include cert fingerprint in metadata

SCIM recommendations:
- Endpoint: https://scim.redwood.ai/atlasbank
- Supported resources: Users, Groups (v2)
- Suggested group schema mapping: orgUnit -> group.name; role -> group.meta.role (we can map based on your existing group UID)
- Bulk provisioning: stick to incremental deltas; we support batch upserts of 100 users per request

Service accounts & tokens:
- Use a namespaced service account (redwood-atlas-prod-provisioner) with scim:write and sso:read roles only; do not grant admin:org privileges
- Token TTL: default 30 days; recommend automation for rotation every 14–30 days depending on Atlas policy

IP allowlist (egress) addresses for Redwood test/staging/prod:
- staging: 34.82.11.45
- prod primary: 54.210.183.9
- prod secondary (failover): 54.210.184.11

I attached a minimal saml-example.xml and scim-schema.json for your identity team to validate. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

—Jonas
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: saml-example.xml, scim-schema.json

Acked — I'll own service-account provisioning. Notes / constraints from infra: 
- Naming: redwood-atlas-<env>-provisioner (env = staging|prod). Example: redwood-atlas-prod-provisioner
- Permissions: scim:write, scim:read, sso:read — no org admin or billing scopes
- Rotation: set up a short-lived token rotation via our secrets manager pipeline. We'll create a CICD job that rotates the token and updates the running service account credential (rotation every 14 days recommended)
- Audit & org policy: we will enable audit logging for the service-account actions; if Atlas requires HSM-backed keys we can escalate to security for a KMS integration

I'll attach a small template for the service-account request (internal) and will create the provisioning ticket by EOD 9/2.
